📌 Address Poisoning: Why Your Transaction History Can Trick You

Main Points
⏺ Scammers send tiny or zero-value transfers from addresses that look like ones you use
⏺ Copying an address from your wallet history can send funds straight to the attacker
⏺ This post explains how address poisoning works and how to avoid it


1️⃣ Core Idea — an attacker creates an address that matches the first and last characters of one you often use, then makes it appear in your transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Works — most wallets shorten addresses to something like 0x12ab…89cd, so a fake with the same start and end looks identical at a glance.
3️⃣ Example — you regularly send USDT to 0x12ab…89cd. A scammer sends you a 0 USDT transfer from a lookalike 0x12ab…89cd. Next time you copy the latest address from history, your funds go to the attacker.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — blockchain transfers can't be reversed, so one wrong paste can mean a permanent loss.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — save trusted addresses in your address book, check the full address, not just the edges, and send a small test transaction before large transfers.
Final Thoughts

Address poisoning doesn't hack your wallet — it hacks your habits. A few extra seconds of checking can save the whole transfer.

🌐 BlackRock sees record Bitcoin whale demand for IBIT conversions despite ETF outflows 

⚠️ BlackRock has reported record demand from large Bitcoin holders seeking to convert their cryptocurrency into shares of its iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), with security concerns driving approximately $3.6 billion in reported transactions. According to Robbie Mitchnick, BlackRock’s head of digital assets, demand for in-kind Bitcoin conversions has continued growing despite recent cryptocurrency price declines. Speaking to Barron’s on November 9, Mitchnick said investors increasingly prefer holding Bitcoin exposure through regulated investment products instead of managing large cryptocurrency balances themselves. 

🚫 The actual amount may be higher because BlackRock does not directly process or track every transaction completed through its intermediaries. Mitchnick described current interest as “the highest we’ve seen at any point”, pointing to continued demand among wealthy individuals and institutional Bitcoin holders. He identified “security and peace of mind” as the main reasons investors request the service, particularly those seeking alternatives to managing private keys and maintaining large cryptocurrency balances in personal wallets.

➡️ Through in-kind conversions, eligible investors transfer existing Bitcoin into the ETF structure and receive shares representing their investment. The transactions involve authorized participants and other approved intermediaries responsible for arranging the creation of ETF shares. BlackRock works with firms including Galaxy Digital, Talos and Virtu to facilitate conversions, while minimum transaction requirements depend on the intermediary.

April 15th, 1861, President Lincoln invoked the Insurrection Act to circumvent posse comitatus, in response to Fort Sumter. Then 12 days later, Lincoln unilaterally suspended the writ of habeas corpus while Congress was out of session (important), citing that he had to act immediately without Congressional approval, in order to suppress the rebellion and defend the public.

Then a few weeks later, in May 1861, a Circuit Court judge ruled that President Lincoln did not have the authority to suspend habeas corpus. Lincoln refused to comply with the ruling, and both he and the Military continued to do what was necessary. Lincoln then proceeded to do what he wanted without Congressional approval for almost two years, until Congress approved that he could suspend habeas corpus, whenever POTUS judged that public safety required it, and this stayed in effect throughout the war.

Lincoln pretty much told the judiciary to fuck off, and he told Congress that he had to act and could not wait for them, and honestly didn’t really need them. Lincoln was going to save the Republic during times of “rebellion or invasion”, and there wasn’t a damn thing anyone was going to do to stop him.

U.S. Pushes for a Final End to Russia-Ukraine War as High-Stakes Talks Resume in Abu Dhabi 🕊

Washington is stepping up efforts to secure a lasting end to the war between Russia and Ukraine as trilateral talks involving U.S., Russian and Ukrainian officials continue in Abu Dhabi. The meetings mark the first serious attempt to revive direct diplomacy since February.

The Trump administration wants an agreement that goes beyond a temporary ceasefire and establishes conditions to prevent another major outbreak of fighting. At the center of the discussions is a potential new European security framework that could reshape relations between Russia and the West for years to come.U.S. officials are reportedly exploring ways to restart dialogue between Moscow and NATO, while also considering possible changes to sanctions as part of a broader settlement. 

Ukraine could receive security guarantees designed to deter future Russian aggression, with some proposals drawing comparisons to NATO's Article 5 collective defense commitment. But Kyiv is looking for more than diplomatic assurances. Ukrainian officials want concrete, enforceable protections that would prevent Russia from launching another invasion once a deal is signed. European governments are also watching the negotiations closely. 

Several capitals fear Washington and Moscow could reach an understanding without giving European allies a meaningful role in shaping the outcome. Any agreement that limits NATO's military presence in Eastern Europe would likely face strong opposition. Russia has repeatedly called for a major overhaul of Europe's security architecture, including restrictions on NATO's military infrastructure. 

Western governments rejected those demands before Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. The Abu Dhabi talks are expected to continue Wednesday. 

The challenge for negotiators is clear: finding a settlement that Ukraine can accept without creating new security risks for Europe. Whether Washington can turn diplomatic momentum into a lasting peace remains uncertain.

📌 Pi Network rolls out 4 developer updates ahead of November summit 

➡️ Pi Network has released four updates covering app development, token tracking, AI-assisted software packaging, and identity verification ahead of its Nov. 17–19 Ecosystem Summit.Inside the Developer Portal, a dedicated App Configuration section has replaced the previous onboarding checklist. Developers can manage domains, API keys, app wallets, and privacy information from the same area.

📊 Navigation now provides clearer routes to services including Pi Sign-In, Ecosystem Listing, PiNet and the Pi Ad Network, according to the team. For approved applications, local storage lets preferences and session information remain on a user’s device. Pi said the data stays off its servers, although it remains tied to the particular account and device and does not automatically follow users across devices.

On November 12, 2025, the United States Mint in Philadelphia struck the last 1-cent coin made for circulation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Treasurer Brandon Beach were there for the final strike. New collector versions will still be made in limited quantities, but no new pennies are being produced for everyday change.

The Mint reported losing $85.3 million making pennies in fiscal 2024. Pennies remain legal tender. Abraham Lincoln has been on the one-cent coin since 1909, the 100th anniversary of his birth.
